_note: exp-036 run plan, committed BEFORE the run (issue #50 follow-up / issue #49: every fine-tune claim so far is Mistral-only). exp-036 replicates exp-026 (pool-only QLoRA fine-tune, 250 steps, fp16 evaluation on the ADR 0007 pinned 600) with ONE change: the base model, mistral_7b_instruct -> qwen3_5_9b. Every hyperparameter comes from the UNEDITED shared configs (configs/finetune_decomposer.json, configs/decomposer_musique.json, configs/musique_eval.json); the only CLI difference from exp-026 is --model qwen3_5_9b on the training command and --model qwen3_5_9b on the evaluation command. notebooks/exp-036_qwen_pool_ft_colab.ipynb and experiments/exp-036/compare.py read this file, so the commands, the input hashes and the comparison families live in one place. Nothing in this file is a measured result of exp-036: numbers marked 'estimate' are estimates, every other number is a setting or a hash already recorded by exp-026 / exp-027 / exp-032.
seed_source: exp-026 trained and evaluated with seed 42 (experiments/exp-026/config.json training_run_config.seed and decomposer_run_config.seed); configs/finetune_decomposer.json seed is 42.

consequences_of_the_change_not_separable: prompt: the model folder's own prompt_unguided.md (Qwen chat template, system/user split on <<<USER>>>, enable_thinking=false) instead of Mistral's plain prompt - the same rule exp-026 followed (train on the prompting arm's own prompt file with the few-shot block empty), so the prompt shape moves with the model folder, as it did between exp-020 and exp-027.

LoRA coverage: configs/finetune_decomposer.json lora.target_modules is kept byte-identical (q/k/v/o/gate/up/down_proj). Qwen3.5-9B has 32 decoder layers of which 8 are full attention (q/k/v/o_proj) and 24 are Gated DeltaNet linear attention (in_proj_qkv / in_proj_z / in_proj_b / in_proj_a / out_proj - read from transformers 5.5.4 models/qwen3_5/modeling_qwen3_5.py); every layer has gate/up/down_proj. So the identical list adapts attention in 8 of 32 layers and the MLP in all 32. Expected trainable count from the HF config (r=16; derived, NOT measured): 8 x (q 196,608 + k 81,920 + v 81,920 + o 131,072) + 32 x 3 x 262,144 = 29,097,984, vs exp-026's measured 41,943,040. The run measures it (trainable_parameters in metrics.json). Adding the linear-attention projections would be a second change; it is not made here.

stop token: the Qwen tokenizer's eos_token is <|im_end|> (id 248046); trl 1.10 appends tokenizer.eos_token to every completion and run_decomposer.generate stops on tokenizer.eos_token_id, so training and inference agree on the stop token (checked on CPU with the real tokenizer at the pinned revision: 2,000 rows, max 222 tokens incl. eos, 0 over max_length 1024).

model-folder settings that differ (components/decomposer/models/*/config.json, read 2026-11-27): post_process.strip_think true (Qwen) vs false (Mistral) - fires only if a <think> block is emitted; exp-027 measured 0/600 such rows with enable_thinking=false. loader.trust_remote_code true (Qwen folder, inference) vs false (Mistral) - the Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B hub repo ships no modeling code and transformers 5.5.4 registers qwen3_5 natively, so it selects no different code; training uses configs/finetune_decomposer.json loader.trust_remote_code false for both. generation.max_new_tokens 256 vs 128 in the folders, overridden to 1024 for both by configs/decomposer_musique.json generation_overrides.

compute dtype: identical across the two models - training bnb_4bit_compute_dtype bfloat16 and bf16 autocast (configs/finetune_decomposer.json); fp16 eval loads the base in float16 (both folders' cuda_dtype); the 4-bit eval uses run_decomposer.load_model's hard-coded bnb compute dtype float16 (exp-026 had no 4-bit eval; exp-027 used the same path). Qwen3.5 was trained in bfloat16, so float16 inference carries an overflow risk Mistral's run did not test; eval.gate.output_health is the pre-declared check.

model.hf_revision_note: The hub's main on 2026-11-27 (HF API: latest commit 2026-03-02 'Update README.md'; no commit since). exp-027 (2026-09-20) and exp-005 (2026-08-19) ran after that date, so they loaded these weights unless their cache predates 2026-03-01 - unverifiable from here. The pipeline loads by model_id without a revision, so the notebook downloads main and REFUSES to continue if main no longer resolves to this sha.
model.runtime_parameter_count_source: exp-027 log row, [model_size] line (AutoModelForCausalLM loads the text model only; the 9,653,104,368 safetensors total includes the vision tower).
model.fla_fast_path: NOT installed, on purpose: exp-027 ran Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet on the torch fallback ('The fast path is not available ... Falling back to torch implementation', runs/exp-027/run.log). Installing flash-linear-attention / causal-conv1d would change the kernel the comparator ran on.

inputs._note: Both are loaded from the existing artifacts, never rebuilt (ADR 0035 amendment: pool construction depends on CPython random.sample, so a rebuild under another Python could differ). Paths are relative to the repo's runs/ root. sha256 values are the ones exp-026 recorded; verified again on the laptop copy on 2026-11-27 (sha256sum, both match).

musique_official_reference._note: reference/musique_official under the data root. Not in git; not read by the decomposition evaluator (only src/answer_metrics.py cites it). Fetched from the pinned upstream commit; sha256s equal the archived copies (verified 2026-11-27).

eval._note: 4bit is the PRIMARY evaluation (mandatory): it is the precision-matched side of pair (b), the fine-tuning gain on Qwen3.5-9B against exp-027 (Qwen3.5-9B prompting on this pool, 4-bit); no fp16 Qwen3.5-9B prompting arm exists on this pool. fp16 replicates exp-026's evaluation protocol exactly (quantization none = the folder's cuda_dtype float16, --no-few-shot, same retrieval artifact for the query set) and serves pair (a) vs exp-026 and the context pairs; it runs after the 4-bit eval, so an fp16 failure (memory on an L4, or the output-health gate) cannot cost the primary. PRECISION ASYMMETRY, stated wherever the two families' gains are set side by side: the Mistral reference gain (exp-026 vs exp-015) is fp16 vs fp16; the Qwen gain (pair b) is 4-bit vs 4-bit. {adapter} is filled by the notebook from the training run directory.

fp16.role: secondary - replicates exp-026's evaluation protocol; serves pair (a) and the context pairs

4bit.role: PRIMARY - precision-matched to exp-027 (4-bit prompting); mandatory

output_health._note: Pre-declared before the run (review I-4): catches fp16 overflow / NaN logits and all-empty outputs. Applied to both evaluations.
output_health.max_rows_with_empty_decomposition_source: exp-027 (same base model, 4-bit prompting, same 600): rows_with_empty_decomposition = 1 in runs/exp-027/decomposer/20260920_102503/metrics.json (read 2026-11-27; exp-026: 0).
output_health.degenerate_definition: a row whose decomposition_raw contains a run of 8 '!' characters. '!' is token id 0 of the Qwen3.5 tokenizer (checked at the pinned revision), which is what greedy argmax returns over all-NaN logits - the signature of an fp16 overflow. exp-026 and exp-027 results.json: 0 such rows each (checked 2026-11-27).

compare._note: CPU side, run on the laptop after the per-item files are copied back: experiments/exp-036/compare.py. Comparator per-item files are exp-032's re-parsed re-evaluations (scaffold-label parser of PR #61, evaluator at 5c4e442; exp-026 and exp-027 changed 0/600 rows under the re-parse, exp-015 7/600 - the re-parsed reading is the one a new-parser run is compared against, ADR 0039; git diff 5c4e442..HEAD is empty for scripts/ and src/), so all sides are scored by the same evaluator code. Families are fixed here, before any exp-036 p-value exists (ADR 0036 item 5); revised 2026-11-27 after code review, still before any run.

a_family_contrast.framing: SECONDARY: same recipe, same data, same eval protocol and precision (fp16); the base model moves (family, generation AND size: 8.95B vs 7.25B runtime params; LoRA coverage differs by architecture, ADR 0044) - it places the second model's fine-tune beside the first, not a one-factor family effect.

b_finetune_gain_qwen.framing: PRIMARY for 'does the fine-tuning gain hold for a second family': the fine-tuning gain on Qwen3.5-9B - same base model, same precision (4-bit), same 600; what moves is adapter + zero-shot prompt vs no adapter + 5 retrieved exemplars. The Mistral analogue is exp-026 vs exp-015, which is fp16 vs fp16: the two gains are measured at different precisions.

c_context_fp16_vs_exp027.framing: CONTEXT ONLY, PRECISION DIFFERS (fp16 vs 4-bit) - the shape of exp-026 vs exp-020.

d_context_precision_on_adapter.framing: CONTEXT ONLY: the same adapter at fp16 vs 4-bit; says how much the precision of pair (b) matters.

compare.holm_p_basis: ADR 0036 item 3: exact McNemar p for binary metrics (break_exact_match, hop_count_exact_match, under/over_decomposition), paired-t p for continuous (sari, ged, chain_validity); the bootstrap CI is reported beside it and any disagreement is disclosed. F3 uses the paired t for all seven (see difference_of_differences).

difference_of_differences._note: The cross-family claim. Per item i of the shared pinned 600 and per metric: DoD_i = (exp036_4bit_i - exp027_i) - (exp026_i - exp015_i), i.e. the Qwen fine-tuning gain minus the Mistral fine-tuning gain on the same question. Paired percentile bootstrap (the evaluator's _paired_bootstrap, resampling items jointly, seed 42, 10,000 iterations) on the two per-item gain vectors gives the CI of mean(DoD); the Holm p is the paired t over the per-item gains (= one-sample t of DoD vs 0) for every metric, binary ones included, because exact McNemar is not defined for a difference of differences. For lower-is-better metrics (ged, under/over_decomposition) a NEGATIVE DoD means the Qwen gain is the larger. PRECISION ASYMMETRY: the Qwen gain is 4-bit vs 4-bit, the Mistral gain fp16 vs fp16. Without this family, any cross-family statement is only qualitative sign agreement of the two gains, and must be worded so.

gpu._note: Requirement the notebook enforces before anything loads. Peak numbers below for exp-036 are ESTIMATES (not measured) scaled from measured exp-026 / exp-027 / exp-030 peaks; the run measures them.
gpu.estimate_train_peak_gib: 12-14 (estimate): 4-bit linears ~3.5-3.7 GB + embed_tokens and lm_head (each 248,320 x 4,096, untied) upcast to fp32 by peft prepare_model_for_kbit_training ~8.1 GB + LoRA/optimizer/activations ~0.5-1 GB. Mistral's 32,768-row vocab is why exp-026 peaked at 5 GiB.
gpu.estimate_eval_fp16_peak_gib: 18-19.5 (estimate): 8,953,803,264 params x 2 bytes = 16.7 GiB + adapter + ~0.6 GiB overhead (exp-026: 14,438 MiB for 7.25B).
gpu.estimate_eval_4bit_peak_gib: ~8 (estimate; exp-027 measured 8,026 MiB for the same base at 4-bit without an adapter).
gpu.requirement_text: A GPU with >= 22 GiB visible memory AND bf16 support (compute capability >= 8.0): training is bf16 QLoRA (configs/finetune_decomposer.json training.bf16=true) and the binding step is the (secondary) fp16 evaluation at ~18-19.5 GiB (estimate). Colab L4 (24 GB, sm_89) and A100 (40/80 GB, sm_80) pass; T4 (16 GB, sm_75, no bf16) and V100 (16 GB, sm_70) fail.

wall_clock_estimate._note: ESTIMATES, not measurements. Base: exp-026 on an RTX 3090 - training 1,568.8 s (250 steps), fp16 generation 842.3 s over 600 queries; exp-027 4-bit Qwen3.5-9B generation 1,655.1 s (few-shot prompts ~375 tokens, so an upper bound for the zero-shot adapter eval). Factors: x1.23 for parameters (8.95B / 7.25B); x1-2 for Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet running on the torch fallback (unmeasured for training); GPU vs 3090: training A100 x0.5-0.7, L4 x1.3-2.5; fp16 decoding (bandwidth-bound) A100 x0.5-0.6, L4 x2.5-3.1 (L4 ~300 GB/s vs the 3090's ~936 GB/s); 4-bit eval taken as 20-28 min on a 3090 (exp-027's 27.6 min with longer few-shot prompts is the upper end; the torch-fallback cost is already inside that measurement), then A100 x0.6, L4 x1.3-2. Setup (venv, data extraction, ~19 GB model download) not included: add ~15-30 min.

T4.note: not supported: fails the VRAM and bf16 gate
